Consider the security of the delivery destination, particularly if you request a file containing journal content or detailed religious study activity.

title: 51. Erasure, withdrawal, restriction, and objection
paragraphs: Depending on applicable law and the circumstances, you can request deletion, withdraw a consent, ask for processing to be restricted, or object to a use. These actions have different effects. Withdrawing waiting-list consent ends the stated launch-notification use; it does not automatically delete the app account. Turning off public streak display changes visibility; it does not necessarily remove the underlying private progress record.

Erasure can be available through the in-app account process or a verified request. Some retained information may be necessary for a legal obligation, security investigation, or another limited lawful purpose. The team should explain any applicable exception rather than treating a general retention statement as permission to keep everything indefinitely. Withdrawal does not necessarily make an earlier lawful use unlawful, but it affects future processing based on that consent.

A restriction request should identify the information and disputed use. For example, you might want a directory contact temporarily hidden while authority to publish it is checked. An objection should explain the relevant processing and concern without requiring you to reveal more sensitive details than necessary. Rights requests must not be used to delete another person's account or suppress accurate information simply because you disagree with their beliefs. The team should verify the request and balance applicable obligations fairly, while giving you a clear explanation of the outcome and any available escalation route.

title: 52. Portability and usable exports
paragraphs: Where applicable law provides a right to data portability, you can request eligible information in an appropriate structured format and, where applicable, ask for transmission to another provider. The scope depends on the legal basis, manner of processing, and information involved. The app's study-journal export is a useful product feature, but it should not be described as automatically satisfying every possible statutory portability request.

An export may contain local records, account-linked data, or selected study content according to the feature. It may not include all authentication-provider metadata, diagnostic logs, administrative records, or information held by an independent map service. A readable archive also does not necessarily preserve every application relationship, content licence, or future compatibility requirement. Ask the team if you need a specific category beyond what the product export contains.

Check the destination and encryption format before accepting an export. A file useful for portability can also expose private content if stored in a public folder or forwarded to the wrong recipient. Portability concerns your eligible information; it does not provide a right to obtain another person's private notes, unrestricted directory databases, or secret operational credentials. If a file unexpectedly includes another user's record, stop using it and report the issue. Keep exported copies secure and manage them separately after an account deletion, because the service cannot automatically recall independent backups you chose to create.

title: 53. Complaints and supervisory authorities
paragraphs: If you think personal information has been handled incorrectly, first identify the relevant feature, record, or request and contact the privacy team. Explain the concern and desired outcome. The team should assess the facts and respond through an appropriate private channel. You do not need to publish your journal or religious circumstances publicly to raise a complaint.

In South Africa, you may have the right to raise a POPIA-related complaint with the Information Regulator. Where the GDPR applies, a competent data-protection supervisory authority may also provide a complaint route. Other jurisdictions can have their own regulators and rights. Use the authority's current official website for forms, contact details, and procedures rather than relying on an outdated address copied into a long policy.

A complaint route is available independently of whether the team agrees with your interpretation. The team should not discourage a lawful complaint or require you to waive applicable rights as a condition of ordinary support. Some disputes may involve an independent church, map provider, email provider, or app store rather than processing controlled by exégeomai. In those cases, the team can explain the boundary and direct you to the relevant organisation where appropriate. Keep records of your request and response, while avoiding unnecessary replication of sensitive attachments. The policy's length does not itself establish regulatory approval or legal compliance.

title: 54. Changes, new features, and future integrations
paragraphs: A large application can evolve, but potential future capabilities are not automatically part of today's processing. If a new feature introduces purchases, remote messaging, additional analytics, recording, or a new public audience, its data handling should be explained before users rely on it. We do not use hypothetical features to justify collecting information for unspecified future purposes.

Changes can include a new provider, altered synchronisation behaviour, a different privacy default, or a new use of existing information. The team should update the notice and relevant feature prompts, and obtain an appropriate choice where required. A revised effective date should identify a genuine change rather than silently reusing a policy that no longer matches the released application. Old builds may continue to behave differently until users update, so release configuration matters.

If you notice a permission prompt or data flow not covered clearly here, pause the optional interaction and contact the team with the app version and feature name. You can continue using unaffected features where available. A notice update does not authorise the app to make private journal content public without the relevant basis and controls. Similarly, a new terms clause cannot override mandatory privacy rights. We aim for a policy that remains understandable through a summary, table of contents, detailed feature explanations, and practical examples rather than making users find a new disclosure hidden in unrelated legal text.

title: 55. Example: studying offline and reconnecting later
paragraphs: Suppose you sign in while connected, download a translation, and then study without a connection during a journey. Opening the downloaded chapter can use local content. Saving a favourite or completing a study item can create a local account-linked action. If the action is eligible for synchronisation, the durable queue can preserve it and submit it when the account reconnects. These are three distinct steps: content retrieval, offline activity, and later account transmission.

If you want the relevant study activity to remain local, review the private-study choices before recording it. Merely switching off Wi-Fi postpones communication; it does not express a permanent instruction never to synchronise. A mobile-data connection can also reconnect an apparently offline device. Check the actual connectivity and privacy state rather than relying only on whether one network icon is visible.

The downloaded translation provider can have a delivery log even though your subsequent chapter reading was local. The account service can have the synchronised favourite after reconnection even though it was first created offline. A manually exported journal can have a separate copy again. If you later request deletion, identify the account records you want removed and manage your own exported copy. This example explains why the policy distinguishes local reading, queue persistence, content delivery, and cloud storage instead of using a single “offline” label to describe all four. The same distinction applies to notes and highlights where those features use a synchronisation path.

title: 56. Example: hiding a milestone without deleting your progress
paragraphs: Suppose you earned a study milestone and want to keep the progress privately without showing it to others. The relevant public-streak or achievement visibility control can change the presentation in supported community features. Your private account can still need the underlying achievement identifier and progress state to display the milestone to you. Hiding the public display and deleting the private record are different choices.

Check for a successful server confirmation when you change public visibility. If the connection fails, the previous public setting may still govern the server. A local switch movement is not sufficient evidence that another user can no longer see the old display. If the app reports an error, retry through the supported flow or ask the team for assistance. Do not publish a screenshot of the entire account to prove the problem; a redacted explanation and the relevant setting are usually enough.

Someone who saw the milestone earlier may retain an independent screenshot. The team can change service-controlled visibility but cannot promise to erase every copy made by another person. If the earlier display contains inaccurate or sensitive information, explain that in the request. You can ask to correct the milestone, hide it, remove the record, or delete the account, and should specify which outcome you want. Choosing one should not silently be treated as authorisation for all the others. Consider whether your avatar and username still identify you even after a progress indicator is hidden.

title: 57. Example: replacing an identifiable avatar
paragraphs: Suppose you uploaded a photograph and later decide to use an illustration. Editing the profile can replace the current image reference with the new selection. The old photograph may have had a public storage URL and may have been downloaded or cached by another person. Replacing the current avatar therefore changes an important display, but it does not necessarily prove that the old object and every independent copy are gone.

Ask for removal of the old avatar if that is your goal. Identify the account and approximate replacement time without sending a high-resolution copy of the photograph unnecessarily. If you still have the old URL, provide it through the private request channel rather than posting it publicly. The team can investigate the object it controls and explain any relevant cache or retention boundary. If another person appears in the image, mention that permission or privacy concern without disclosing unrelated details about them.

Revoking photo-library permission after the upload prevents future selection through that permission, but does not retract the server upload. Deleting the source image from the phone's gallery is also a separate action. These distinctions help you choose an effective privacy response. For a future avatar, select a neutral image if recognising your face or location would be uncomfortable. Check the background as well as the main subject, since signs, uniforms, vehicles, or a distinctive residence can identify someone even when the face is partly obscured.

title: 58. Example: registering a homecell at a private residence
paragraphs: Suppose an organiser wants to list a homecell that meets in someone's home. The directory form can accept a location, leader, schedule, and contact details. Publishing the exact location can help invited visitors, but it can also expose a family residence to people outside the intended group. The ability to enter the address is not evidence that the homeowner approved public publication.

Before submitting, obtain appropriate authority and decide what detail is suitable for the public directory. An organisational contact and broader town description may be sufficient if an exact address should be given only to confirmed visitors. Do not include children's names, private household phone numbers, or sensitive pastoral notes in the public description. Verify that the map pin does not accidentally identify a neighbouring residence. A geocoding result can be inaccurate even when it looks precise.

The address search may send the query to an external provider before the listing is saved. Cancelling the directory submission can prevent publication in the app while leaving that separate provider interaction unaffected. If a residence has already been published without permission, contact the team with the listing identifier and request an appropriate correction or removal. Explain any immediate safety concern without adding it to the public listing. The team should distinguish the public directory record, the contributor's account, and external mapping records when explaining what can be changed.

title: 59. Example: correcting a directory contact
paragraphs: Suppose a ministry listing displays your personal phone number even though you are no longer responsible for that branch. The relevant request is a directory correction or removal of the contact, not necessarily deletion of your personal app account. Your app account and the organisational listing may be stored separately and can have different submitters or administrators.

Identify the ministry, branch, field, and desired correction. If you have a public organisational contact that should replace the number, provide it only if you are authorised to do so. The team may need to verify the correction with an appropriate representative or assess your privacy concern directly. You should not need to surrender your account password or upload an entire identity document simply to flag an obviously private contact appearing in a public record.

If an external website or map directory also displays the number, that independent record may need a separate request to its operator. The exégeomai team can change records it controls and explain any remaining boundary. Keep the request factual: distinguish an outdated contact, an unauthorised publication, and a dispute about ministry ownership. A correction process should not be used to redirect an organisation's visitors to an unrelated private business or impersonator. After the change, review the visible listing when possible and tell the team if the old detail still appears through another service-controlled view or cached result.

title: 60. Example: asking for help with a private note
paragraphs: Suppose a personal study note will not save. A useful report can identify the screen, app version, approximate note size, whether you were connected, and the error shown. The team usually does not need to read the entire reflection to reproduce a save failure. You can create a harmless test note with the same approximate length or explain which input pattern caused the issue.

If a screenshot is necessary, redact names, health information, family circumstances, and other private text. Check whether the screenshot also shows your email, profile image, or another person's record. A small attachment sent privately is generally more suitable than a public repository issue containing your journal. Do not include session tokens or encryption keys in a diagnostic report, even if someone asks for a detailed log.

A support conversation can itself become a personal-information record. The email service and authorised support recipients receive what you attach. Deleting the failed note inside the app does not remove the support attachment. If you want that attachment deleted after the investigation, include that request and ask about any necessary recordkeeping limitation. The team should use a redacted reproduction where possible rather than copying sensitive production notes into a development environment. This example applies equally to an export failure, a bookmark that will not synchronise, or a privacy setting that does not confirm its update.

title: 61. Example: leaving the waiting list and keeping your app account
paragraphs: Suppose you joined the launch waiting list and later created an app account using the same email address. Those records serve different purposes. An unsubscribe request for launch notifications should stop the waiting-list programme for that address without being interpreted automatically as an instruction to erase the app account and its study records.

Email joinus@exegeomai.co.za from the registered address and state that you want to unsubscribe from the launch waiting list. If you also want account deletion, say so separately and use the authenticated in-app process where available. A request involving a new email address may need limited verification so that another person cannot remove or access your records. Do not send the password for either your app account or mailbox.

Confirmation emails and earlier launch messages can remain in your inbox or in operational delivery records even after the active subscription is removed. Your own mailbox copies are under your control. The team should stop the relevant future use and explain any limited retained record needed to honour the unsubscribe or meet applicable obligations. If you receive a message after requesting removal, forward the minimal message information needed to investigate, including the destination address and time, without attaching unrelated personal correspondence. A change to your app's notification settings does not necessarily unsubscribe an email waiting-list entry, because local reminders and launch emails use different systems.

title: 62. Example: deleting an account after exporting a journal
paragraphs: Suppose you export your journal to a personal cloud drive and then delete your app account. The authenticated deletion process concerns the service-controlled account and related records, together with the client cleanup performed after confirmation. Your drive copy was deliberately placed with a separate provider and remains a separate record unless you remove it there.

Before deleting, confirm that the export is usable and stored securely if you intend to keep it. If the archive is encrypted, retain the appropriate access material safely; an account deletion or device reset may affect access to a local key. Do not assume support can reconstruct a lost encryption secret. If you no longer want the backup, remove it from the drive and review that provider's recycle bin, version history, shared links, and retention options.

A recipient who previously received a journal copy may also retain it. You can ask them to remove it, but the application's deletion button cannot automatically erase their independent device. The same applies to printed notes, screenshots, email attachments, and public posts. The team should explain any remaining service-controlled retention when responding to a deletion request, rather than claiming every copy everywhere vanished instantly. If the app reports deletion failure, do not rely on the reset appearance of a local screen alone. Obtain a successful confirmation or contact the team about the account state before assuming the cloud account is gone.

title: 63. Example: a shared device and more than one account
paragraphs: Suppose two family members use the same phone at different times. Each person's account can have different privacy preferences, progress, notes, and synchronisation queues. The application uses account-scoped storage and account checks in relevant paths to reduce mixing, but the device's notification centre, photo library, exported files, and ordinary system access can still be shared.

Sign out through the supported flow before another person signs in, and let important pending actions resolve where possible. Review the new account's privacy and lock settings instead of assuming that the first person's choices apply to everyone. A cached translation can appropriately be common non-personal content, while a private note or account token should not be treated the same way. If another person's note appears unexpectedly, do not save or share it; report the issue with a redacted account-switching description.

The operating system's device lock protects the device, while an app lock protects a particular access path. Neither prevents a person with broad device access from opening an exported file you saved in a shared folder. A biometric enrolment used by several people can also reduce the practical exclusivity of a local lock. Consider separate devices or platform user profiles where available if confidentiality is especially important. After an account deletion or reset, review remaining downloads and independently saved files; not every shared-device record is tied to the account that was just removed.

title: 64. Example: diagnostic reporting without a full journal upload
paragraphs: Suppose the app crashes while displaying a study screen and the release has Sentry configured. The diagnostic integration can submit a crash event and technical context so the team can investigate. The reviewed sanitisation removes several personal and request fields from standard events. That reduction matters, but it does not mean the event contains no information or that every diagnostic event is identical.

A stack trace can identify the failing component, app version, device characteristics, or timing. Sampled performance reporting can have a different event structure from a standard exception. The policy therefore explains diagnostics conditionally and avoids claiming that all network telemetry is absent. It also avoids promising a user-accessible diagnostic opt-out where the installed interface has not implemented one.

If you report the crash manually, do not attach your journal to supplement the automatic event unless a minimal redacted example is necessary and you choose to provide it. Ask about the relevant release configuration if you want to understand whether remote diagnostics were active. A private-study preference controls study paths; it should not be assumed to disable an independent diagnostic integration. Similarly, turning off notifications does not turn off crash reporting. These are separate purposes and controls. The team should review event contents and provider retention rather than relying solely on a comment in the source code or the name of a privacy setting.

title: 65. Example: following an external link from the app
paragraphs: Suppose you open a ministry's website, an external Bible resource, a map link, or an email contact from the app. The destination can receive a request from your browser or selected application and may process technical information, account state already held there, and anything you submit directly. The exégeomai privacy notice does not replace that destination's notice.

A link's presence does not certify the destination's security or authorise it to access your app journal. Check the address before entering credentials or personal information, especially if a page asks you to sign in with an unrelated account. Do not reuse your exégeomai password on a church website or send it to a contact reached through a directory listing. A malicious or outdated destination can have practices different from the legitimate organisation's current site.

If the app's link is wrong, report the listing or screen and destination URL. The team can correct a link it controls, while the external operator remains responsible for its own content and records. A request to remove your details from an external contact form generally needs to go to that operator as well. You can often use a public phone or office email without submitting extra personal details. The choice to contact a ministry is yours; opening a directory record does not mean you consented to unrelated marketing, private counselling records, or indefinite storage by every organisation named in the directory.

title: 66. A final privacy checklist for your own choices
paragraphs: Before using a feature, consider what information it needs, whether the information stays local, whether a cloud or external provider receives it, and whether any part becomes public. This is especially useful for study exports, avatars, precise addresses, public milestones, and directory contacts. The goal is to make a deliberate choice rather than prevent ordinary study. Many educational interactions need little personal detail.

After changing a setting, look for confirmation and understand its scope. A discoverability change is different from account deletion. A private-notes preference is different from disabling all network requests. A revoked photo permission is different from removing an uploaded avatar. A deleted local export is different from deleting the same file from a cloud drive. These distinctions are practical tools for requesting the result you actually want.

Keep your app, device, and account credentials protected, and choose an appropriate private channel for support. If you ask for access or deletion, identify the category and desired outcome without sending passwords or unnecessary sensitive documents. If you discover someone else's information, stop exploring it and report the boundary problem responsibly. If this notice does not answer a concrete question, contact privacy@exegeomai.co.za and name the feature or record involved. The team should provide a clear explanation, investigate inconsistencies, and update the notice when the service changes. Your privacy choices and applicable legal rights do not depend on reading every paragraph of this long-form explanation; the summary, contents, and feature-specific sections are intended to help you find what matters to you.
